title: Introduction to HTML
subtitle: The real foundation every app is built on
description: Understand how the web actually works, what tags, elements and attributes really mean, and build your first structured screen that will become your final complete app.

blocks.text: Welcome - Let's be honest about building apps

Hey, it's your instructor here. I won't bore you with textbook English. You want to build a real app, right? Every app you use daily - WhatsApp, YouTube, even this Code Academy app you are holding - started with what you are about to learn today.

And before we go further - you can write and run code INSIDE this app. Don't just read. Go to Home > Click Menu at the top > Click Practical or Practice. That editor is your lab. Every code I show you today, test it there.
How a website actually becomes visible

When you type google.com, here's what really happens: Your browser (Chrome) asks a server 'give me google's HTML file'. The server sends that file as plain text. Chrome reads that text from top to bottom and draws the page you see. No magic.
That means if you write an HTML file yourself and open it in Chrome, Chrome will treat it as a real website. You don't need internet to start.

blocks.text: What HTML really means - beyond definition

HTML means HyperText Markup Language. HyperText means text that links to other pages - like when you click a button and it takes you to another lesson. Markup means you mark your text to tell the browser what it is.

Imagine you have plain text: 'Welcome'. Is it a heading? A paragraph? A button? Browser doesn't know. But if you write

Welcome

, you MARKED it as a big heading. If you write

Welcome

, you MARKED it as a paragraph. That's markup.
Crucial point: HTML does not do thinking or calculations. It only structures. CSS will handle beauty, JavaScript will handle brain. HTML is the skeleton. Without skeleton, nothing stands.

blocks.text: Tags, Elements, Attributes - Never confuse them again

This is where 90% of beginners get confused, so let me kill the confusion now. A TAG is the < >. Just the brackets. An ELEMENT is the full thing: opening tag + content + closing tag. An ATTRIBUTE is extra information you put INSIDE the opening tag.

blocks.text: Why attributes control your app's behavior

Without attributes, many tags are useless. Take . It means link, but link to where? The href attribute tells it where to go. means image, but which image? src attribute tells which file. alt tells what to show if image fails and helps blind users.

blocks.question: You write Click here without href and it doesn't navigate. A junior says it's a browser bug. What is the REAL critical reason?
options: The <a> element requires an href attribute to define its destination, without it it's an anchor placeholder not a link
The <a> tag is a void element and needs self-closing syntax <a />
The text inside <a> must be inside <head> for navigation to work
The browser requires CSS to make <a> clickable
blocks.correctFeedback: Exactly right. <a> without href is valid but does nothing - it's an empty anchor. The attribute gives it purpose.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Think deeply: What tells the browser WHERE to go? It's the attribute, not CSS or closing syntax.
blocks.reasoning: href is what gives anchor its hyperlink behavior. Without it, it's just a placeholder element.

blocks.text: Let me explain like we are in class: <!DOCTYPE html> tells Chrome 'this is modern HTML5, don't use old rules'. <html lang="en"> is the root container. <head> is INVISIBLE information - title, charset, viewport. <body> is VISIBLE content. If you put <h1> inside <head>, users won't see it properly.

That viewport meta tag is life-saving. Without <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0"> your app will look tiny on phones, zoomed out like desktop. Every app you build must have it.

blocks.question: Two developers built pages. Dev A has viewport meta tag, Dev B doesn't. Both open on a phone and Dev B's page looks tiny and zoomed out. What is the most accurate technical reason?
options: Dev B's page is missing <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0"> which tells mobile browsers to use device width, without it mobile browsers assume 980px desktop width
Dev B forgot <meta charset="UTF-8"> so mobile browsers can't read characters and zoom out
Dev B used <body> instead of <head> for visible content causing mobile scaling issue
Dev B's HTML is missing <!DOCTYPE html> so mobile browsers disable responsive mode
blocks.correctFeedback: Brilliant analysis. Viewport meta is what switches mobile browsers from desktop emulation to responsive mode.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Focus: What meta controls width and scaling on mobile? Charset is about characters, DOCTYPE is about rendering mode, but viewport is about mobile width.
blocks.reasoning: Without viewport meta, mobile browsers render page at ~980px width then shrink it, making it look tiny.

What you actually achieved today

You now understand how browser reads HTML, difference between tag, element and attribute, why void elements don't close, why viewport meta makes your app mobile-ready, why body holds visible content, and you built a screen with h1, p, a, img, hr, br, title, meta.

blocks.question:
You are reviewing a junior's code:

My App

HomeWelcome. The page shows 'Welcome' but h1 is not styled as heading in some browsers and title shows wrong. What are TWO critical errors?
options: <h1> is incorrectly placed inside <head> instead of <body> and <title> should contain only text but its position is affected by the misplaced h1 - visible content must be in body only
<html> is missing lang attribute and <body> is missing viewport meta tag
<h1> should be <head> and <title> should be inside <body> - they swapped them
<title> is a void element and should not have closing tag, and <h1> is also void
blocks.correctFeedback: Outstanding debugging! You found the root cause - head is for metadata only. Visible content like h1 in head breaks rendering and SEO.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Look where h1 is. Is head for visible headings or invisible info? Where must visible elements live?
blocks.reasoning: head must contain only metadata (title, meta, link). Placing h1 in head is invalid and causes unpredictable rendering.
